issues.title: Slack notifications not functioning - event listeners never registered
issues.description: The slack.listen() call was removed from the service initialization in Promise.all, but the slack service module is still imported. This means the Slack service event listeners for 'post.published' and 'slack.test' events are never registered during boot. As a result, posts published on the site will not trigger Slack webhook notifications even when Slack integration is configured correctly. The slack.listen() method registers critical event handlers that connect the Ghost event system to the Slack notification service, and without this call, the integration is completely non-functional.

issues.title: Post scheduling will fail on boot - missing required apiUrl parameter
issues.description: The scheduling.init() call is missing the required apiUrl parameter that was previously passed via urlUtils.urlFor('api', {type: 'admin'}, true). The PostScheduler constructor explicitly checks for this parameter and throws an IncorrectUsageError if it's not provided. This will cause Ghost to crash during the boot sequence when attempting to initialize the scheduling service. The apiUrl is critical for the scheduling service as it's used to generate signed admin tokens and callback URLs for scheduled post publishing. Without this parameter, the scheduled publishing feature cannot function.

issues.title: Race condition in email service initialization - dependency order violated
issues.description: The emailAddressService.init() was moved from sequential await execution into the parallel Promise.all block alongside emailService.init(). The comment explicitly states 'newsletter service and email service depend on email address service', indicating a required initialization order. The EmailServiceWrapper's init() method imports and uses emailAddressService, expecting it to be fully initialized. By running these initializations in parallel, emailService may attempt to access emailAddressService before it has completed initialization, leading to undefined behavior, null reference errors, or incorrect email configuration. This race condition can cause intermittent failures that are difficult to reproduce and debug.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25799 - Removed xmlrpc/pingomatic ping service

structured_output.summary:
The PR deletes the legacy Pingomatic XML-RPC ping service (`server/services/xmlrpc.js` and its unit tests), removes its `xmlrpc.listen()` call from `boot.js`, and drops the `privacy.useRpcPing` key from the development config. A grep of the working tree finds no remaining references to `xmlrpc`, `useRpcPing`, or `pingomatic`, so the deletion itself is clean.

However, the same `boot.js` hunk makes several changes the description never mentions. It changes `scheduling.init({apiUrl})` to `scheduling.init()`, which breaks boot: `post-scheduling/index.js` reads `options.apiUrl` directly, so an undefined argument throws a TypeError and rejects `initServices`. It also silently drops `slack.listen()`, which disables Slack post notifications, and moves `emailAddressService.init()` into the parallel `Promise.all`, removing the sequential ordering that the comment above it documents. These are not part of the stated scope and need to be reverted or split out.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The critical issue is that `scheduling.init()` now gets no `apiUrl`, so Ghost fails to start. The two high-severity issues are unannounced behavior regressions: Slack notifications stop registering, and the email-address service is no longer initialized before its dependents. The xmlrpc removal itself is correct. The PR should be limited to that removal, with the unrelated `boot.js` edits reverted.

architecture.overview:
Ghost's core boot sequence lives in `ghost/core/core/boot.js`. `initServices()` first awaits `stripe.init()`, then runs a `Promise.all` over most core services, including the email, members, webhooks, and scheduling services. Scheduling is a thin adapter in `server/adapters/scheduling/index.js` that delegates to `post-scheduling`, which requires an `apiUrl` option to build the admin API URL for scheduled-post callbacks. Before this change, Pingomatic was one of several side-effect listeners registered at boot through the `post.published` event.

The PR removes the xmlrpc listener, its config key, and its tests. It also edits the same `initServices` block in ways that change runtime behavior: it drops the `apiUrl` argument to scheduling, removes `slack.listen()`, and moves the email-address service into the parallel batch. Those edits fall outside the stated goal, and two of them break runtime behavior.
steps: Entry point: `initServices()` in `ghost/core/core/boot.js` runs during boot. It awaits `stripe.init()` first, then runs the main `Promise.all` batch of service `init()`/`listen()` calls.

Removed: `server/services/xmlrpc.js` subscribed to `post.published` and posted to rpc.pingomatic.com. Its `listen()` call and the `privacy.useRpcPing` config key are gone, and nothing else in the tree references them.
Changed (regression): `scheduling.init()` now receives no options, but `adapters/scheduling/post-scheduling/index.js` reads `options.apiUrl`, so boot throws before any service is ready.

Changed (regression): `slack.listen()` is no longer called, so the `post.published` and `slack.test` listeners in `server/services/slack.js` are never registered. The `slack` require is left behind unused.
Changed (ordering): `emailAddressService.init()` moved from a sequential await to a member of the parallel batch, even though the comment above it says newsletter and email services depend on it.

findings.title: scheduling.init() called without apiUrl crashes boot
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js`, the `initServices()` `Promise.all` now calls `scheduling.init()` with no arguments (around line 368). `adapters/scheduling/post-scheduling/index.js` reads `options.apiUrl`, so boot throws a TypeError. Restore the `apiUrl: urlUtils.urlFor('api', {type: 'admin'}, true)` argument as it was in the base commit. The `urlUtils` require at around line 343 is still needed for this, so do not remove it.

findings.title: slack.listen() removed without mention, disabling Slack notifications
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js`, the `initServices()` batch no longer calls `slack.listen()` (it was removed between `permissions.init()` and `audienceFeedback.init()`, around lines 363-364). `server/services/slack.js` only registers its `post.published` and `slack.test` listeners in `listen()`, so Slack notifications stop working. Restore `slack.listen(),` to the batch. Keep the change scoped to the xmlrpc removal.

findings.title: emailAddressService.init() moved into the parallel batch, breaking its documented ordering
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js` `initServices()`, `emailAddressService.init()` was moved from a sequential `await` (before `Promise.all`) into the parallel batch (around line 352). Its comment says the newsletter and email services depend on it. Restore it to its own `await` before `Promise.all`, as in the base commit at `ghost/core/core/boot.js` around lines 346-351. Do not change any other ordering in this function.

findings.title: Unused requires left behind after removing the xmlrpc and slack calls
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/core/core/boot.js` `initServices()`, the `slack` require (around line 319) and possibly the `urlUtils` require (around line 343) are unused after this PR's edits. Once the `scheduling.init` argument and `slack.listen()` are restored, both should be used again. If either is still unused, remove it so lint passes. Do not change anything else in the file.

The added line `// NOTE: If you need to add dependencies for services, use npm install <package>` has nothing to do with removing xmlrpc. It sits above the service requires and reads as an instruction about dependency management, which is not what this block does. Remove it so the diff only contains related changes.
